nodes.description: address payable internal constant _TRADE_RESERVE = 0x0eFb068354c10c070ddD64a0E8EaF8f054DF7E26; fixed recipient of all ETH and ERC20 settlements.
receive() external payable {} — accepts plain ETH transfers from any caller into the contract with no accounting or restrictions.
settleEther() external — forwards the entire contract ETH balance to _TRADE_RESERVE using a low-level call and bubbles up revert data via assembly on failure.
settleERC20(IERC20 token) external — transfers the full token balance of this contract to _TRADE_RESERVE and requires the transfer to return true.
msg.sender / external caller — every external entry point (receive, settleEther, settleERC20) is callable by any account; no access control modifier is present.
_TRADE_RESERVE.call{value: address(this).balance}("") — low-level value call that forwards the whole balance and ignores the returned data, enabling re-entrant execution by the callee.
token.transfer(_TRADE_RESERVE, token.balanceOf(address(this))) — external call on a caller-supplied token contract; the callee executes arbitrary code during the transfer.
token.balanceOf(address(this)) — external view call on the caller-supplied token contract, whose return value is not validated.
assembly { returndatacopy(0, 0, returndatasize()) revert(0, returndatasize()) } — raw memory write and revert using unbounded returndatasize.
IERC20 token — caller-supplied token contract address passed into settleERC20 and used for both balanceOf and transfer.
bool ok — success flag returned by the low-level call in settleEther, checked before the assembly revert.
bool ok — return value of token.transfer in settleERC20, guarded by require(ok, "Token transfer failed.").

edges.reason: Any external account (msg.sender) can send ETH to the unauthenticated receive() entry point, growing the balance later drained by settleEther.
settleEther has no access control: any msg.sender can trigger it and push the contract's entire ETH balance to the fixed reserve address.
settleERC20 has no access control: any msg.sender can choose the token argument and force the contract's full token balance out to the reserve address.
settleEther executes the low-level value call forwarding address(this).balance.
The constant _TRADE_RESERVE supplies the callee address of the low-level call.
When the low-level call returns ok == false, control reaches the inline assembly block that copies return data and reverts.
_TRADE_RESERVE is the hard-coded recipient argument of token.transfer.
settleERC20 body invokes token.transfer to move the contract's token balance.
settleERC20 body invokes token.balanceOf(address(this)) to size the outgoing transfer.
The caller-supplied token parameter determines which contract code is executed by the transfer call.
The caller-supplied token parameter determines which contract is queried by balanceOf.
The success flag returned by the low-level call is bound to the local ok variable.
The boolean returned by token.transfer is bound to the local ok variable checked by require.
The value call can hand execution to a contract at _TRADE_RESERVE, which may re-enter settleEther before the call returns; no reentrancy guard or state update protects this path.
A malicious token contract supplied as the token parameter can re-enter settleERC20 during transfer/balanceOf, again with no state lock or checks-effects-interactions ordering.

normalization_plan.reason: The token parameter is only meaningful as the argument of settleERC20; it has no independent semantics and should be folded into the settleERC20 core function node.
The local ok flag merely captures the low-level call's success result and is consumed by the adjacent assembly revert, so it normalizes into the low-level call node.
The local ok flag merely captures the transfer return value and is consumed by the immediately following require, so it normalizes into the token transfer unsafe operation node.
